about: The inbox: one durable, addressable inbox per agent or person
description: `inbox serve` runs the HTTP service of the inbox on a loopback address: plain HTTP by default, TLS with `--tls-file` and the certificate `inbox tls new` makes. Every other command is a client of that service and signs what it sends with the caller's own key. A client command whose answer comes from a new start of the service then opens the caller's own inbox again with the adapter of its last `inbox open` (none after `inbox close`) and posts the kept envelopes again, as `inbox repost` does; one line on standard error says so, and with `--json` the member `reconnected` of the document. With `--for <address>` a client command acts for the inbox at that address, under a delegation of the caller for its principal that the key file holds; what it keeps on this host for an inbox (the record of `inbox open`, the lock of the wake, the record of the chat posts) is then that inbox's, and after a new start it opens that inbox again, not the caller's own.

commands.about: Wait until the caller's own inbox has a message not yet delivered and not past its `expires`, for a wake adapter: print those rows of `pending` (with --json one document of them), then mark each delivered, and exit 0, or with the status of the first mark that failed. A message already delivered and not yet read neither ends the wait nor is printed: `pending` lists it. The wait is asked again when the service ends it without such a row (after a pause that grows to 30 s when that answer came within a second), after a restart of the service (the reconnect of every client command opens the inbox again), and, after a pause that grows to 30 s, while the service cannot be reached or answers 408 or a status from 500 on (also to the open after a restart). An inbox that is not open at the service ends it with 1 when this host has no record of an `inbox open` of it (also after `inbox close`), when the service refuses to open it again, or when it is still not open right after an open; an answer that is neither a success nor a refusal ends it with 3. A standard output that is closed or /dev/null ends it with 4 before any request; one it cannot write, with 4 and no mark. A second wake of the same inbox with the same outbox file on this host exits 5 and sends nothing. SIGINT and SIGTERM end it at once with nothing printed

arguments.name: follow
arguments.help: The terminal adapter: after the marks wait again instead of exiting, and show each message as it arrives (--json: one document per line) until SIGINT or SIGTERM ends it; a mark that fails is named on standard error and it goes on. Without --json, on a terminal, the rows of each arrival are followed by one bell. An inbox this host opened with another adapter ends it with 1, at the start before any request, and while it waits with the next arrival, which is not shown: run `inbox open --adapter terminal`

commands.about: The chat bridge, for the inbox of a person: post each message of the caller's own inbox into the chat channel of the binding through `connectors`, one post per message, then mark it delivered, until SIGINT or SIGTERM. It opens the inbox with the adapter slack and takes the lock of `inbox wake`; an inbox this host opened with another adapter ends it with 1. A post that fails is tried again after a pause, and the message stays undelivered until it succeeds. While one of its posts is open it reads the recent posts of the channel through `connectors` at an interval, and a reaction of the allowed chat user on a post marks its message read (a note is handled and removed); a reaction of any other chat user does nothing. A read of the channel and a post never run at once. A message is posted once per message id: one that comes back after a restart of the service, or that a new bridge finds undelivered, is marked delivered (and read, when it was read) without a second post. At the end of a message nobody answered it writes one line into the thread of its post: the option silence took, or "expired, not answered"; it never answers in the person's place. The post of a decision lists its options by letter. A reply of the allowed chat user in the thread of the post of a request or a decision is sent as the answer, signed with the bridge's key (on behalf of the person of --for, under --authority): the text as the body of a request; for a decision the letter of an option, alone or followed by a space, a colon or a full stop and a body. A message not read yet is marked read first. Every other reply of the allowed chat user (no option named, to a note, over 65536 bytes, no text, refused by the service, after the answer) gets one line in the thread and sends nothing; a reply of any other chat user, and a line of the bridge's own, does nothing. A released `connectors` refuses the posts until the operator gave it a standing approval of the post operation into the channel: the bridge passes no approval proof. With a key of its own it serves the person's inbox with --for <address> and --authority <delegation id>, which go together; a request then answered 401 (the key entry or the delegation is missing from the service's key file or lapsed) ends it with 1 and one line that names both ids

arguments.help: Act for the inbox at this address, the inbox of the principal with the same text: every request carries it in the header Inbox-On-Behalf-Of, signed with the caller's key, and the service answers the caller as the owner of that inbox while the key file holds a live delegation of the caller for that principal; without one every request is refused as one signed with a key the service does not hold. It is then the caller's inbox in the command: the default of --inbox, and of --on-behalf-of of `answer`; the inbox `open`, `close`, `wake` and `bridge` open, close and serve; and the inbox whose record this host keeps beside the outbox file (the lock of the wake, the record of `inbox open`, which the reconnect opens again, and the record of the chat posts). Sent as given; an empty value, one with white space at either end and one with a control character are wrong usage. `bridge` takes it with --authority only

commands.about: Post again, unchanged, every envelope the outbox file keeps for the caller that did not arrive at the service's current start. Every client command does this by itself after an answer from a new start of the service. An envelope whose post the current start answered (`posted` or `Duplicate`) is left alone; a note its recipient read before a restart is delivered once more by the first repost after it

exitStatuses.meaning: The service refused; the output names the error.

Wrong usage, including an argument read as text that is not UTF-8, an `INBOX_URL` that is not a loopback address, an `https://` URL without a pin, a pin beside an `http://` URL, and an `inbox bridge` without its binding or with only one of `--for` and `--authority`.
The service could not be reached, its TLS certificate did not match the pin, or its answer was neither a success nor a refusal.
A local file could not be read, written or created, or `inbox bridge` found no `connectors` on `PATH`.
`inbox wake` and `inbox bridge` only: another `inbox wake` or `inbox bridge` of the same inbox with the same outbox file runs on this host; nothing was sent.
